_comment: DECLARED STATUS ONLY. Nothing here is a count, and nothing here restates a fact that
can be read from source. Counts, file existence and evidence results are DERIVED by
scripts/project_capabilities.py, which reads the repository. Recording a count here
would create a second copy able to disagree with the first, which is the drift this
register exists to stop.
What belongs here is the judgement a human makes and a script cannot: whether a phase
is complete, whether a gate is open, whether a feature is deferred. Every one of these
is checked against derived evidence, and a declaration the evidence contradicts fails
scripts/check_project_capabilities.py.
JSON rather than YAML because the repository-checks CI job runs on a bare interpreter
with nothing installed, and PyYAML is not in the standard library. The config/*.yaml
profiles are read by the application, which has its dependencies.

gates._comment: Verdicts are parsed from the readiness documents; these declare the intent.

_comment: ADR-0008 accepts either path. 'pending' until an engine has actually executed the
model; 'passed' requires a non-null validated_at AND a model_source_hash matching
the current TMDL. Declaring 'passed' without both fails the check.
What a reader would look for and not find. Checked against derived counts.
TWO EXCEL ENTRIES, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME DELIVERABLE. excel_operating_report
is P2.4-03: the workbook built over the SYNTHETIC warehouse whose reconciliation
total must match PostgreSQL and Power BI. It is deferred because that
reconciliation needs report pages that do not exist. inventory_operating_report is
the SANITIZED PUBLIC LISTING workbook (ADR-0011), exported from the listing
reporting views by src/arpi/inventory/report.py. It does not reconcile to Power BI
and never will on its own: no DAX measure reads that lane. Declaring one says
nothing about the other, and check_project_capabilities.py holds each to its own
evidence so a reader cannot take the shipped one as proof the deferred one landed.
THREE DEPLOYMENTS, NOT ONE. The portfolio website, the analytical platform and the
semantic model are separate claims with separate evidence, and a status here is
checked against deployment/evidence/portfolio_deployment.json rather than believed.
Asserting 'deployed' without an evidence record fails the check, and so does denying
a deployment the evidence records.
'declared' means the resource is described in source-controlled configuration and
has never been created. It is not a weaker form of 'deployed'.
The review metadata LIMITATIONS.md renders in its header. It lives here rather than in
the document because a hand-typed review date is the first thing to go stale, and a
limitations register whose own header is stale has already lost the argument. The
header is a generated block, so the two cannot disagree.
last_verified_commit is the commit the register's evidence was last read at, and it is
what a limitation's 'last verified' means: not when somebody looked, but which state
of the repository the finding describes.
Prose statements that were true once and are contradicted by the repository now.
Each entry names a claim that must NOT appear, the derived fact that refutes it, and
the files that carried it. scripts/check_project_capabilities.py greps for the
patterns and fails when one reappears.
These are semantic checks, not a banned-phrase list: each is guarded by the evidence
that makes it false, so if the evidence ever goes away the check retires itself
rather than forbidding a statement that has become true again.
